decision.interpretation: Retain for the demonstrated ownership reduction and narrower representation, with no whole-compiler CPU speedup claim. Initial parse-page and append timings are slightly lower overall, while the initial independent-unit run is higher; unchanged-binary confirmation reverses that independent-unit result (median 13.983→13.028 ms, minima 8.515→8.278 ms), so it is not a reproducible regression. Initial full-compile medians are about2–3% higher; per-invocation alternating confirmation gives length compile median1749.351→1749.193 ms and integer-constant compile2087.985→2101.111 ms. Corresponding user-CPU medians differ by+0.59% and+0.09%, with large variation in individual pairs. This evidence does not establish a stable CPU benefit or a material repeatable consumer regression. All observations, including slow runs and tails, remain retained. Three diagnostic samples did not support attributing the initial full-compile difference to integer formatting. The allocation removal and exact behavior comparisons are the acceptance basis; CPU effects remain uncertain on this shared host.
